title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics
authors: Julianna Piskorz*, Antonin Berthon*, Mihaela van der Schaar (* equal contribution)
date: 28 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version on 19 October 2026)
code_note: No code, checkpoints or logs are released and the paper links none; the reproducibility statement points to the appendix's settings instead

code_alt.title: On-policy distillation (Thinking Machines, the recipe this study tests)

takeaway: In controlled strong-to-weak distillation, the token-level KL direction, not who wrote the rollouts, shapes performance and coverage: forward KL is robust to rollout policy, reverse KL favours student rollouts, and the on-policy generalisation edge does not reliably survive later RLVR.
verdict: Believe the main finding for the setting it tested: in matched three-seed comparisons (1B students, answers of about 100 tokens), KL direction and learning rate explain more than who wrote the rollouts, and the gradient argument for why forward KL shrugs off the rollout policy is correct. Treat the side results (the on-policy generalisation edge, the RLVR follow-up, the Spanish style test, the long-answer MATH run) as suggestive: one benchmark, one seed, or a best checkpoint picked on the test set, and the text sometimes describes its own figures more favourably than they read.

resources.by: Thinking Machines (Lu and Thinking Machines Lab), 2025
resources.n: The recipe that made on-policy distillation popular: per-token reverse KL from one sampled token, used as an RL advantage. The paper's sampled-KL ablation (Appendix A.2) tests this estimator.

resources.t: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models (GKD), arXiv 2306.13649
resources.n: Where student-generated rollouts for distillation, and the idea of choosing the divergence separately, come from.

resources.t: When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? (Semi-OPD), arXiv 2610.11291
resources.n: Rollouts the initial student wrote once, reused, beat full on-policy distillation in 14 of 17 teacher-student pairs; on-policy helps only when the pair is well aligned. Same direction as this paper, from a different angle.

resources.t: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation, arXiv 2610.03185
resources.n: On-policy distillation read as RL against the teacher's implicit reward: it makes correct answers easier to sample, and collapses into long repetitive text when that reward is wrong.

resources.t: The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination (RIDE), arXiv 2609.36484
resources.n: Distils in representation space along the RL-induced shift of the teacher instead of matching its next-token distribution.

resources.t: Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models, arXiv 2505.11711
resources.n: The sparse-update claim this paper tests, and whose checkpoints' learning rates its Appendix E lists.

resources.t: RL's Razor: Why Online Reinforcement Learning Forgets Less, arXiv 2509.04259
resources.n: The forgetting claim this paper tests: on-policy training forgets less than SFT.
The generalisation claim this paper tests, made by comparing SFT with RL.

kb.n: The page that owns distillation. Its "Forward or reverse KL" section animates mass-covering against mode-seeking; its "Whose text" section and toy tab run forward and reverse KL on teacher and student text. This paper page links them rather than repeating them.
On-policy distillation in a production recipe: the small Qwen3 models were distilled on their own rollouts after an off-policy stage.

kb.t: RL for LLMs: RLHF, GRPO, RLVR

Strong-to-weak distillation of reasoning by plain SFT on teacher answers, the off-policy end of the spectrum.
